verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's docs emphasize a single native C++ inference core with thin per-platform bindings and hardware acceleration (NPU/Metal), which implies a lightweight, fast-starting runtime rather than a heavy interpreted stack, but there is no direct benchmark or claim about cold-start time before first token compared to alternatives. Community threads discuss token-per-second throughput comparisons (uzu vs MetalRT) but never address startup/cold-start latency specifically. missing for 10: explicit cold-start latency numbers, binary size figures, or first-token time benchmarks versus other runtimes.
